transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um, so the main reason I’m here is... well, work is just getting really difficult lately. Anything that takes real, you know, sitting-down brain work? I just can't seem to do it. Like the monthly reports I have to run, or when I'm supposed to be planning a multi-site health event... which, actually, we just had a big one over at the west campus last week and the parking situation was a complete nightmare. The city decided to repave the main lot the exact same day we launched. Can you believe that? I had to park like three blocks away and I completely scuffed up my good shoes walking through the grass. I just bought these loafers, too, they were supposed to be scuff-proof. 

But, um... right, why I'm here. Yeah, the planning. When I have to actually sit down at my desk and map out the logistics or crunch the numbers for those reports, it feels like I just hit a physical wall. I keep putting it off and putting it off, even when I know it really matters for the clinics and my job's on the line. I just end up finding a million other things to do instead.
Do you feel anxious when you think about doing these tasks or sitting down to work on them?

Anxious? Um... no, I wouldn't really say I feel anxious or nervous about them. My heart isn't pounding or anything. It's more just this overwhelming urge to do literally anything else. 

Like, yesterday I was supposed to start the budget variance report, and instead, I spent an hour and a half cleaning out the staff breakroom fridge. Which, honestly, was long overdue. Someone left a plastic container of what I think used to be chicken Alfredo in the back for at least a month. I ended up just throwing the whole container in the trash because the smell was... well, you just can't get that out of plastic, you know? My wife actually switched us to those glass meal-prep containers at home for that exact reason. They're a lot heavier to carry in my briefcase, but they don't hold onto smells or get those weird tomato sauce stains. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the work tasks. Yeah, no, not anxious. I just don't do them.
Do you have trouble paying attention to details in your work or other activities?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's like... I'll send out a clinic staffing schedule, or even an email for the kids' soccer league—I help coach my son's team, the Tornadoes. Well, they wanted to be the Sharks, but there was already a Sharks team in the older division, so we had to pivot. Anyway, I'll send these emails out, thinking I double-checked everything. I swear I look at it. But then someone will reply and point out I put the wrong date, or I left off the location for the game entirely. 

Which is a huge pain, because then you have parents texting you at 8:00 AM on a Saturday asking what field we're on, and I'm usually trying to wrangle the equipment bags. We just got these new pop-up goals that are supposed to fold up really easily, but they never do. You have to twist them in this weird figure-eight motion, and if you don't get it exactly right, they just spring back open. It's ridiculous. 

But yeah, I miss stuff like that all the time. Details I definitely would have caught before, I just... I don't know, my brain just skips right over them.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Restless? Um... no, not really. I mean, I sit still okay. I'm not, you know, bouncing my leg or tapping my fingers constantly or anything. I can sit through a whole meeting, usually. 

Well, unless the chairs are those awful hard plastic ones. We had those in the conference room at the east wing clinic until last month. I finally got them to approve a budget to swap them out for the mesh ergonomic ones. Best decision ever. The mesh breathes so much better, especially in the summer when the AC in that building decides to just... stop working. It happens every July like clockwork. The maintenance guys say it's because the compressor is on the roof and gets direct sun, but I told them they should just build a little awning over it. My neighbor did that for his home unit, built this whole little wooden trellis thing with vines growing on it. It looks really nice, actually. He grows jasmine, so his whole patio smells amazing in the evening. We tried growing jasmine once, but our dog kept digging it up. He's a terrier mix, you know, so digging is just in his blood. 

But, um... wait, restless. No, I don't think I'm restless. I just sit there. My mind might be a million miles away, but my body is pretty still.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Impulsive? Um, no, I wouldn't say so. I don't really do things without thinking. If anything, I probably overthink things sometimes. 

Like when we were picking out the new tile for the master bathroom. I must have brought home twenty different samples. We were trying to decide between this slate gray and a warmer beige tone. The beige looked better with the vanity, but the gray hid dirt better. And with the dog—the terrier mix I mentioned—he tracks in so much mud. We have this little paw-washer cup thing that you fill with water and stick his paw in, which works great, except he hates it. He tries to bite the silicone bristles. My wife found it on one of those social media ads, and usually I don't trust those things. I bought a laser measurer from an ad once, and it was off by like three inches every time. I tried to use it to measure the clinic waiting room for new rugs, and they ended up being way too small. Looked like bath mats sitting in the middle of the floor. We had to send them all back, which was a nightmare because the return shipping wasn't covered. 

But no, I don't really act on impulse. I usually think things through pretty carefully.
Do you feel upset or discouraged about not being able to complete your work tasks?

Yeah, I do. It's really frustrating. I mean, I'm still getting by at work, and I'm still doing all my community stuff, but... it's just getting embarrassing. I've had to make so many last-minute apologies to my coworkers, and even my friends, because deadlines keep slipping. People are having to cover gaps for me. 

Like last week, my assistant had to pull together the quarterly compliance report because I just... I couldn't get it finished. And she's already so busy. She's planning her wedding right now, actually. It's going to be at this beautiful vineyard out in the valley. We went wine tasting out there for our anniversary a couple of years ago. They have this amazing Pinot Noir. I don't usually drink red wine because it gives me a headache—something about the tannins, I think. My brother-in-law makes his own beer in his garage, and he says it's the sulfites, but I don't know. He made this IPA last month that was so hoppy it tasted like pine needles. I couldn't even finish a glass. I poured it into the sink when he wasn't looking. 

But yeah, it's just... I hate that I keep dropping the ball. It makes me feel like I'm not doing my job right.
Do you find yourself making careless mistakes in your daily activities?

Careless mistakes? Um... yeah, actually. That happens more than I'd like to admit lately. I'll send out the clinic staffing schedule for the week, or an email for the kids' soccer league—I help coordinate the under-12 division—and I'll think I've checked it over perfectly. But then someone will reply and point out that I put the wrong date, or I completely left off the location for a game. Stuff I definitely would have caught before. 

The soccer league thing has been especially stressful this season because they changed the field assignments. We used to always play at Centennial Park, which was great because they have that little concession stand with the good pretzels. You know, the big soft ones with the salt? My youngest loves those. But now they've moved us to the new complex on the south side of town, and the parking there is just a nightmare. It's all gravel, and when it rains, it turns into a complete mud pit. I had to get my car detailed twice last month just to get the mud out of the floor mats. The guy at the car wash said I should invest in those heavy-duty rubber mats. He tried to sell me a set for like two hundred bucks, but I found them online for half that. Same brand and everything. Shipping took forever, though. I think it got stuck at a facility in Ohio for a week. 

But um, yeah, the mistakes. Like leaving off details on the schedule. It's just... I look right at it and somehow miss it until someone else points it out.
Are you having trouble with your relationships with family or friends because of your difficulties with work tasks?

Trouble with relationships? No, not really. I mean, my wife gets a little annoyed sometimes when I bring work stress home, but who doesn't, right? We're actually doing pretty well. We just celebrated our anniversary, actually. We went to this Italian place downtown that just opened up. The food was incredible. I had this osso buco that was just... falling off the bone. But the parking down there is ridiculous. They have valet, but it's like thirty dollars, and I just can't bring myself to pay that when I can walk three blocks for free. Although, it was raining that night, so my wife wasn't too thrilled about the walk. She had these new suede shoes on, and she was so worried about ruining them. Have you ever tried that waterproofing spray for shoes? I bought a can of it last winter for my boots, but it smelled so strongly of chemicals I had to leave them in the garage for three days before I could wear them. And then I think it actually changed the color of the leather a little bit. They were supposed to be this dark chocolate brown, but now they look almost black in certain lighting. 

But no, my relationships are fine. The work stuff is just mostly affecting me, I guess.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Yeah, all the time. It's actually getting pretty bad at the clinic. Like, we have these weekly meetings, and I'll be sitting there trying to listen to the budget update—which is already dry enough as it is—but then someone's phone vibrates on the table. Or I hear people talking out in the hallway. Or I'll just suddenly remember something I forgot to do for the soccer league, like ordering the end-of-season trophies. 

We used to get those little plastic gold cups, you know? The ones on the faux-marble bases. But last year, one of the parents complained that they looked cheap, so we switched to these custom medals. They're actually really nice, they have the kids' names engraved on the back. The only problem is the guy who does the engraving is located two towns over, and his shop hours are terrible. He's only open from like ten to three on weekdays, which is exactly when I'm at work. I had to take an extended lunch break just to pick them up last season, and I ended up getting a flat tire on the way back. I ran over a giant nail right outside this construction site. It was one of those massive roofing nails. The guy at the tire shop said it went straight through the sidewall, so they couldn't even patch it. I had to buy a whole new tire, and of course, they tell you that you should really replace them in pairs so the tread matches. So a quick trip for medals ended up costing me like four hundred dollars. 

But anyway, yeah, in the meetings... if a thought like that pops into my head, or I hear a noise, I just get pulled away. And by the time I tune back in, I've completely missed the last few minutes of what they were saying.
Are you finding it harder to manage your daily routine because of these difficulties with work tasks?

Manage my daily routine? Um... I mean, I'm still getting by, mostly. Like, I'm showing up and doing my job at the clinic, and I'm still handling the soccer stuff, but... it's definitely getting harder. I've had a few deadlines slip lately, which is so frustrating. And people have had to step in and cover gaps for me. Like last week, I completely forgot to submit the payroll approval on time, and our HR rep had to rush it through manually so people would get paid on Friday. I felt terrible. I had to send out all these embarrassing, last-minute apologies to my coworkers. 

It's just like... I'm dropping the ball more. I even had to apologize to one of my good friends, Dave, because I was supposed to help him move a couch on Saturday morning and I completely blanked on it. I didn't remember until he called me at noon asking where I was. Speaking of couches, we actually just bought a new one for our living room. My wife wanted one of those big sectionals with the chaise lounge on the end. We went to this huge furniture warehouse out by the interstate. It's one of those places where you have to walk through like a maze to see everything, like IKEA but without the meatballs. We spent three hours in there. We finally picked out this really nice gray one, but they told us it was out of stock and we'd have to wait six weeks for delivery. Six weeks! And then, when they finally did deliver it, the guys couldn't get it through our front door. They had to take it around back and hoist it over the deck railing. It was a whole production. One of the guys actually scraped his arm pretty bad on the brick siding. I offered him a band-aid, but he just wrapped a paper towel around it and kept going. 

But yeah, the routine... I'm keeping my head above water, I guess, but it's taking a toll. I'm just constantly apologizing to people for things slipping through the cracks.
Did you have difficulties with paying attention or completing tasks when you were a child?

Yeah, actually... it's kind of always been like this. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers were always telling my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just constantly daydreaming. I'd be staring out the window instead of looking at the chalkboard. And I was always losing my worksheets. I'd just shove them in my desk and they'd get crumpled up into these little accordions. I'd forget to turn in my homework all the time unless my mom literally went through my backpack every single night to check. 

Backpacks were so different back then, too. Remember those heavy canvas ones with the leather bottoms? Jansport, I think. I had this bright blue one that I covered in patches. My dad actually helped me iron them on. He had this old, heavy iron that weighed like ten pounds, and he'd always complain about the cord getting tangled. We had this one patch from a family trip to the Grand Canyon. We drove all the way there in this massive station wagon with the fake wood paneling on the sides. My sister and I sat in that rear-facing third row, making faces at the cars behind us. It was so hot that summer, and the AC in that car was terrible. We had to roll the windows down, and the wind was so loud you couldn't even hear the radio. 

But yeah, the school stuff... I was always forgetting things, losing papers. My mom really had to stay on top of me just so I'd get my work turned in.
Did you have a lot of extra energy as a child, like you were always running around or had trouble sitting still?

Extra energy? Um... no, not really. I wasn't really the bouncy type, you know? I didn't get in trouble for running around the classroom or jumping off the furniture or anything like that. I was pretty quiet, honestly. Just kind of... in my own world. 

My sister, though, she was the one bouncing off the walls. She did gymnastics for years. She was always doing cartwheels in the living room and knocking things over. She actually broke my mom's favorite lamp once doing a handstand against the wall. It was this really ugly, tall ceramic thing with painted sunflowers on it that my mom got at a flea market. She loved going to flea markets on Sunday mornings. We used to have to get up at like 6 AM to go with her, and she'd haggle over a dollar for some dusty old teacup. I hated going because the grass at the fairgrounds where they held it was always wet with dew, and my sneakers would get completely soaked. I had these cheap canvas shoes that took forever to dry out, and they always smelled a little like mildew afterward. 

But yeah, anyway, no... I wasn't hyper. I didn't have trouble sitting still, I just had trouble paying attention to what I was supposed to be looking at while I was sitting there.
Have you always had difficulty with tasks and paying attention, or did it start happening more recently?

Well, I mean, like I said about school, the daydreaming and losing papers has always been there in the background. But it getting this bad? This hard to manage? That's more recent. It's been going on for, I'd say, about a year and 11 months now. That's when my friend died, and I ended up taking on a lot more of the soccer league stuff and the community outreach responsibilities. 

He was the one who actually started the league, you know? We used to play together in this adult rec league on Thursday nights. It was under the lights at the high school stadium, which always made it feel way more official than it actually was. The turf there was awful, though. Those little black rubber pellets would get everywhere. I'd take off my cleats in the garage and literally pour a handful of them out of each shoe. My wife used to get so mad because I'd track them into the house and she'd find them in the laundry room or on the carpet. We have this really light beige carpet in the hallway upstairs, which was a terrible choice in hindsight. Any little speck of dirt shows up on it. We've tried everything to keep it clean—we even bought one of those fancy steam cleaners that looks like a small spaceship. It has all these different attachments that I never know how to use. The manual for it is like a novel, and it's translated into like twelve different languages. 

But yeah... the real struggle, the dropping the ball and things slipping through the cracks at work, that really ramped up almost two years ago when I took on his share of the league stuff.
Are you finding that your difficulties with tasks and attention are affecting your hobbies or leisure activities?

Well, with my hobbies, like the soccer league... yeah, it's definitely bleeding into that. I mean, I'm still getting by at work and with the community stuff, but it's getting messy. People are having to cover my gaps, and deadlines are slipping past me. I've had to make so many embarrassing last-minute apologies to coworkers and friends because I just drop the ball. 

Speaking of dropping the ball, we actually had to order new ones for the league last month. The old ones were getting completely waterlogged because it rained for like three straight weeks this spring. It was that really fine, misty rain that doesn't seem like much but completely soaks you to the bone if you're out in it for more than five minutes. My raincoat is completely useless against it. I bought it at this outdoor supply store that was going out of business, so it was like seventy percent off, but I think they sold me a defective one. The zipper always gets stuck right around the collarbone area, and I have to yank it so hard I feel like I'm going to rip the fabric. I should probably just throw it away and get a new one, but you know how it is, you just keep putting off buying things like that until you absolutely need them. 

But yeah... it's definitely affecting things. The apologies are getting pretty old, honestly. I just feel like I'm always scrambling to catch up.
Are you feeling like your difficulties with tasks and attention are affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah, I mean... it definitely takes a toll. Like I was saying before, I'm still getting by at work, you know, managing the clinic, and I'm still doing the community stuff. But it's... it's just exhausting. People are having to cover my gaps more and more. Deadlines slip right past me before I even realize they were coming up. I've had to make so many of those embarrassing last-minute apologies to my coworkers and friends. 

It's actually really awkward at the clinic because I'm the one who's supposed to be managing the schedule and making sure everything runs smoothly. We just switched to this new electronic health record system, and it is an absolute nightmare. The interface looks like it was designed in 1998. Everything is gray and blocky, and you have to click through like six different screens just to update a patient's phone number. The IT guy who came to train us on it was this kid who looked like he was maybe nineteen, and he kept talking so fast and using all this jargon. He brought in these donuts for the staff, though, which was nice. They were from that little bakery on Main Street, the one with the pink awning? They make these incredible maple bacon bars. My wife hates bacon on sweet things, she says it's an abomination, but I think the salty and sweet combination is perfect. We actually got into a whole debate about it at a dinner party last month. 

But yeah... the apologies. It just makes me feel like I'm letting everyone down, you know? It's definitely affecting how I feel about my life right now.
Do you feel like your difficulties with tasks and attention are affecting how you feel about yourself?

I mean... I'm not really sure. I haven't really stopped to analyze it like that. I don't think it fundamentally changes how I feel about myself as a person, I'm just... annoyed that I keep messing up. 

Actually, speaking of how I look at myself, we just had to take new headshots for the clinic's directory last week. Corporate decided the old ones looked too dated. They hired this local photographer who brought in all these massive reflective umbrellas and bright lights, and he set up a whole makeshift studio right in the middle of our breakroom. It completely blocked the microwave, which was a huge pain because I had brought leftover lasagna for lunch that day. My wife makes this incredible lasagna—she puts a layer of ricotta mixed with spinach in the middle. It sounds kind of weird if you don't like greens, but it actually balances out the acidity of the tomato sauce perfectly. She uses those no-boil noodles, too, which I guess saves a ton of prep time. 

I tried making it myself once when she was out of town visiting her sister in Ohio. Her sister just had her first baby, a little boy. They named him Arthur, which is kind of cute but also feels like a really old name for a baby, you know? Like you almost expect a baby named Arthur to come out wearing a little tweed suit and carrying a briefcase. I bought them this little stuffed elephant as a gift, but the shipping got delayed so it arrived like two weeks after they got home from the hospital. 

But anyway, the photographer kept telling me to tilt my chin down and smile naturally, and all I could think about was my cold lasagna sitting on my desk. So I haven't really noticed a big shift in my self-esteem or anything, just mostly that lingering frustration with the daily slip-ups.
Have you always had these difficulties with tasks and attention, or did they start or significantly worsen at some point in your life?

Well, yeah, it's pretty much always been like this. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always tell my parents at conferences that I was bright, but I was just constantly daydreaming. I was always losing worksheets, and I'd forget to turn in my homework unless my mom physically went through my backpack every single night to check. 

Actually, speaking of my old backpacks, my mom kept this one I had in third grade. It was bright blue with the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles on it. Leonardo was always my favorite because he had the swords, you know? But the zipper on that backpack broke halfway through the year, so my mom used these giant safety pins to keep it closed. She was always really resourceful like that. She grew up on a farm in Iowa, so she learned how to fix just about anything with whatever was lying around. They grew mostly corn, but they had this huge vegetable garden out back where they grew the most amazing tomatoes. I try to grow tomatoes in my backyard now, but the squirrels always get to them right before they ripen. It's infuriating. I even bought this special netting to put over the plants, but those little guys just chew right through it. I saw this video online where a guy built a whole enclosure out of PVC pipe and chicken wire to protect his garden, and I've been meaning to go to the hardware store to get the supplies for it, but I just haven't gotten around to it yet. 

But yeah, the daydreaming and losing stuff... that's been happening since I was a kid. It's not really a new thing at all.
Do you think your main problem is that you have trouble focusing on tasks or that you get distracted and move on to other things?

I think it's... well, it's definitely the getting distracted part. It's like my attention just gets hijacked. Like, if I'm in a meeting at the clinic, and I'm really trying to listen to the budget update—which, honestly, is the driest part of the week—if someone's phone vibrates on the table, or I hear people talking out in the hallway, I'm just gone. Or even if I just suddenly remember something I forgot to do for the community league, my brain just completely leaves the room, and I miss the next few minutes of whatever they were saying.

Speaking of the league, we're trying to organize this summer barbecue fundraiser right now, and it's been a whole ordeal trying to secure the park permits. The city council changed the application process this year, and everything has to be submitted through this new online portal. It reminds me of that terrible new system at the clinic I was telling you about. I don't know why every organization suddenly decided they needed to upgrade their software this year, but it's like they all hired the same company that specializes in making things as confusing as possible. 

I was actually talking to my neighbor, Dave, about it the other day while we were taking out the trash. Dave's a retired software engineer, so he always has these really strong opinions about user interfaces. He was telling me about how back in the early days of the internet, they had to code everything by hand using HTML. He has this massive collection of vintage computers in his basement, like old Commodores and Apple IIs. He invited me down to see them once, and it smells exactly like an old library down there. It's kind of comforting, honestly. He was showing me this game called Oregon Trail on one of them, which I vaguely remember playing in elementary school. I always used to die of dysentery before I even made it halfway across the map. I guess I wasn't very good at managing my supplies, which is pretty ironic considering my job now. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the focus thing. Yeah, it's definitely the distractions that get me. My brain just grabs onto whatever the newest, shiniest thing is, even if it's just a thought in my own head, and the thing I'm supposed to be doing just vanishes.
Do you find it difficult to focus and stay on task in your personal life, outside of work and the soccer league?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into everything else. I mean, even just with the neighborhood stuff, I've been forgetting to return calls from volunteers, and I keep missing small errands for events. Like, once or twice I've had to apologize because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me asking where I was. 

Actually, the last time that happened, I was right in the middle of trying to fix the ice maker on our fridge. It just stopped making ice one day, and my wife loves ice water. She has this giant insulated tumbler that she carries everywhere. It's one of those really popular ones that comes in all the pastel colors—hers is seafoam green. Anyway, I was watching this YouTube tutorial on how to test the water inlet valve, and the guy in the video had this incredibly thick Boston accent. It was almost distracting how strong it was. He kept saying "wahtah" instead of water. My college roommate was from Boston, actually. He used to make us watch the Red Sox games every time they were on, even if we had a huge exam the next day. He was a good guy, though. He ended up moving to Seattle and opening a coffee shop, which is funny because he used to drink those terrible energy drinks all through school. 

But yeah, I was knee-deep in the fridge manual when my phone buzzed, and it was Dave asking if I was logging onto the neighborhood watch Zoom call. I felt terrible, I just completely forgot it was Thursday. So yeah, the forgetfulness is definitely a problem outside of work too.
Have you been experiencing these difficulties with attention and tasks for at least 6 months?

Yeah, definitely more than six months. It's been... gosh, probably about a year and eleven months now that it's been this bad. That's when my friend passed away, and I ended up taking on a lot more of his responsibilities for the soccer league and the community outreach stuff. 

He was actually the one who originally got me involved in the league. We played on the same adult rec team for years. We were both terrible, honestly, but we had a blast. He played goalie, and he had this ridiculous neon orange jersey that he insisted was lucky. He claimed it blinded the strikers when they were trying to take a shot. I don't know if it actually worked, but we did make it to the semi-finals one year, mostly because the other teams kept getting disqualified for not having enough players show up. Adult rec leagues are so flaky like that. People sign up in the spring when the weather is nice, but by July, no one wants to run around in the ninety-degree heat. I can't really blame them. I bought these special cooling towels last summer that you soak in water and snap, and they get ice cold. They actually work really well, but I keep forgetting to put them back in my gym bag after I wash them. 

But anyway, yeah, since he died and I took over all the scheduling and the outreach coordination on top of my clinic job, it's just been completely overwhelming. That's when I really started noticing how much I was dropping the ball on everything.

patient.answer:
Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. Um, so the main reason I’m here is... well, work is just getting really difficult lately. Anything that takes real, you know, sitting-down brain work? I just can't seem to do it. Like the monthly reports I have to run, or when I'm supposed to be planning a multi-site health event... which, actually, we just had a big one over at the west campus last week and the parking situation was a complete nightmare. I just bought these loafers, too, they were supposed to be scuff-proof. 

But, um... right, why I'm here. Yeah, the planning. When I have to actually sit down at my desk and map out the logistics or crunch the numbers for those reports, it feels like I just hit a physical wall. I keep putting it off and putting it off, even when I know it really matters for the clinics and my job's on the line. I just end up finding a million other things to do instead.

patient.answer:
Anxious? Um... no, I wouldn't really say I feel anxious or nervous about them. My heart isn't pounding or anything. It's more just this overwhelming urge to do literally anything else. 

Like, yesterday I was supposed to start the budget variance report, and instead, I spent an hour and a half cleaning out the staff breakroom fridge. Which, honestly, was long overdue. Like, once or twice I've had to apologize because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me asking where I was. 

Actually, the last time that happened, I was right in the middle of trying to fix the ice maker on our fridge. It just stopped making ice one day, and my wife loves ice water. She has this giant insulated tumbler that she carries everywhere. It's one of those really popular ones that comes in all the pastel colors—hers is seafoam green. Anyway, I was watching this YouTube tutorial on how to test the water inlet valve, and the guy in the video had this incredibly thick Boston accent. It was almost distracting how strong it was. He kept saying "wahtah" instead of water. My college roommate was from Boston, actually. He used to make us watch the Red Sox games every time they were on, even if we had a huge exam the next day. He was a good guy, though. He ended up moving to Seattle and opening a coffee shop, which is funny because he used to drink those terrible energy drinks all through school. 

But yeah, I was knee-deep in the fridge manual when my phone buzzed, and it was Dave asking if I was logging onto the neighborhood watch Zoom call. I felt terrible, I just completely forgot it was Thursday. So yeah, the forgetfulness is definitely a problem outside of work too.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms meet criteria for inattention being present for at least 6 months
doctor.question: Have you been experiencing these difficulties with attention and tasks for at least 6 months?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 11 months, since my friend died and I took on more of the league and outreach responsibilities.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms have been present for at least 6 months, which directly relates to the duration of my symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely more than six months. It's been... gosh, probably about a year and eleven months now that it's been this bad. That's when my friend passed away, and I ended up taking on a lot more of his responsibilities for the soccer league and the community outreach stuff. 

He was actually the one who originally got me involved in the league. We played on the same adult rec team for years. We were both terrible, honestly, but we had a blast. He played goalie, and he had this ridiculous neon orange jersey that he insisted was lucky. He claimed it blinded the strikers when they were trying to take a shot. I don't know if it actually worked, but we did make it to the semi-finals one year, mostly because the other teams kept getting disqualified for not having enough players show up. Adult rec leagues are so flaky like that. People sign up in the spring when the weather is nice, but by July, no one wants to run around in the ninety-degree heat. I can't really blame them. I bought these special cooling towels last summer that you soak in water and snap, and they get ice cold. They actually work really well, but I keep forgetting to put them back in my gym bag after I wash them. 

But anyway, yeah, since he died and I took over all the scheduling and the outreach coordination on top of my clinic job, it's just been completely overwhelming. That's when I really started noticing how much I was dropping the ball on everything.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, disorganization, and difficulty with task completion, which have been persistent since childhood and have recently worsened, are most consistent with a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), predominantly inattentive type.
